MachineryEquipment.title: Key Machinery and Equipment in the Port

gantryCrane.title: Gantry Crane - Container Lifting Crane at the Dock with Straight Travel
gantryCrane.content: Used for lifting containers on and off feeder vessels, capable of efficiently moving containers and easily positioning them as the containers are locked onto the crane arm and moved along the rails attached to the arm.

jibCrane.title: Jib Crane - Container Lifting Crane at the Dock with Rotating Function
jibCrane.content: Used for lifting containers on and off barge vessels, as the barge is a smaller vessel with a limited number of containers. The rotating container lifting crane is stationed at both of Sahathai Port’s barge docks, with one unit at each dock. Additionally, BBT has two rotating container lifting cranes at its barge docks.

rtg.title: RTG - Rubber-Tyred Gantry Crane for Container Yard Lifting
rtg.content: Designed for efficient space management, this crane allows containers to be stacked in multiple layers and ensures accurate placement, helping reduce costs and time spent in moving stacked containers.

mobileHarborCrane.title: Mobile Harbor Crane - Mobile Dock Crane
mobileHarborCrane.content: This crane supplements the gantry crane at the dock, especially when there is a high volume of container handling. It is flexible in operation as it can move like a crane truck, aiding in the transportation of containers to various points within the feeder port area.

reachStacker.title: Reach Stacker - Container Lifting Truck
reachStacker.content: Our reach stacker can lift cargo weighing up to 42 tons, efficiently transporting containers within the dock area.

emptyContainerHandler.title: Empty Container Handler
emptyContainerHandler.content: Our terminal efficiently and quickly manages large empty containers.

tractorTrailer.title: Tractor and Trailer
tractorTrailer.content: Our tractors can quickly move containers, coupled with strong and durable trailers, ensuring safe transportation of containers throughout the journey.

forklift.title: Forklift
forklift.content: To manage goods efficiently, we have 13 forklifts to help handle goods within Sahathai’s warehouse areas quickly and safely.

Ocr.title: Automatic Cargo Container Reading Technology (OCR)
Ocr.content: Sahathai Terminal has collaborated with organizations in the country to develop an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) system for reading cargo container numbers at the port entrance. The use of OCR technology improves operational efficiency and smoothness, increases accuracy in verification, and reduces processing time, allowing customers to receive faster and higher-quality service.

FreeTradeZone.content: Located just 200 meters from Sahathai Terminal, the total area covers 6,400 square meters.

Facilitate.content: Specially designed for smoother cargo handling and easier docking operations.

docking.title: Berth Allocations
docking.content1: Shipping lines or their agents must email the details of the cargo vessel, services, and characteristics of the cargo vessel (general storage plan, ship securing plan, cold storage container placement plan, safety systems, and container space schedule) to Sahathai Terminal at least one week in advance before docking.
docking.content2: The shipping line or agent must send the long-term docking schedule at least one month in advance to Sahathai Terminal so that the terminal can plan the container booking in advance by 7, 3, and 1 day before docking. The shipping line or agent must also send an estimated docking date (ETA) and the approximate amount of cargo to be loaded or unloaded so that Sahathai Terminal can confirm the docking plan (POB) and the estimated departure date (ETD) of the vessel.

operatingHours.title: Operating Hours
operatingHours.content2: General containers transported by truck: 24 hours before Actual Time of Berthing (ATB)
operatingHours.content3: Reefer containers (fruit cargo): 1 hour before ATB
operatingHours.content4: Dangerous goods, Group 2 (DG GROUP2): transported directly from vessel/chassis to chassis/vessel
operatingHours.content5: Dangerous goods, Group 3 (DG GROUP3): can be stored at the port for up to 48 hours after being unloaded from the vessel, or 48 hours before the operating time of the Container Freight Station (CFS) at origin
operatingHours.content6: If overtime work is required, it must be notified before 16:00 on a working day
operatingHours.content7: CFS cargo cut-off time: 6 hours before the CY cargo cut-off time

CfsGoodsContent.title1: Sahathai Terminal accepts the following CFS/LCL cargo
CfsGoodsContent.content1_1: Goods packed in packaging or on pallets weighing no more than 2 tons, which can be lifted by forklift.
CfsGoodsContent.content1_2: For goods packed in packaging or on pallets weighing more than 2 tons, please contact our Customer Relations department to inform us of your request.
CfsGoodsContent.content1_3: Additional charges will apply if special equipment or tools are required for storing the goods.
CfsGoodsContent.title2: Sahathai Terminal does not accept the following CFS/LCL cargo
CfsGoodsContent.content2_1: Goods that may cause pollution at the port or warehouse, such as powder or molten chemical substances.
CfsGoodsContent.content2_2: Goods prohibited by government agencies, such as certain types of dangerous goods (DG).
CfsGoodsContent.content2_3: Heavy equipment, imbalanced goods, and other goods that cannot be lifted by forklift and/or require special lifting equipment.
CfsGoodsContent.content2_4: Sahathai Terminal reserves the right to provide additional equipment and personnel for special cargo handling cases. In such cases, the cargo owner must arrange their own lifting equipment and personnel.
CfsGoodsContent.title3: Regulations for goods packed in wooden packaging at the destination country
CfsGoodsContent.content3_1: If regulations regarding wooden packaging must be specified, customers must notify Sahathai Terminal at the time of booking.

safetyRegulations.title: Safety Regulations
safetyRegulations.description: Thailand is a signatory to the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea 1974, as amended 2002, which requires vessels and ports to follow security protocols to prevent threats and ensure safety. Sahathai Terminal has developed a security plan in compliance with the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. The terminal is committed to preventing various threats such as theft, drug smuggling, stowaways, piracy, terrorism, sabotage, hijacking, kidnapping, arson, assassination, and other security risks. A security plan and risk assessments have been submitted to the Marine Department for approval and certification.

hazardousGoods.title: Hazardous Goods
hazardousGoods.description:
Hazardous goods are identified and classified using the UN Number. The goods are divided into three categories:
Category 1: No unloading.
Category 2: Not accepted for storage; customers must pick up the goods at the side of the vessel.
Category 3: Can be stored for up to 5 working days; customers must pick up within 5 days of the container being placed in the yard.
For further information, users can check the UN Number using the following system:
https://stt.sahathaiterminal.com/containerinquery/Default.aspx?type=DG

requestPermissionContact.title: Visitor Access
requestPermissionContact.description:
For access to Sahathai Terminal's port area by external visitors:
1) If a visitor wants to meet port staff, security must follow the control procedure for entering and exiting the port area.
2) If the visitor is meeting port staff, security will evaluate the appropriateness of the visit and issue a pass after verifying identity with an ID card or government-issued document. Visitors must obtain a permission slip and get it signed by the staff they are visiting.
3) After the visit, visitors must return their pass. If access to the terminal’s office buildings is required, visitors must follow the access control procedures.
4) Contractors working temporarily on the premises must follow the same procedures to obtain a work permit and follow the security protocols.

DocumentProcess.content1: The shipping line or its agent must submit information via EDI (Baplie)/CASP and a list of special cargo to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA). The shipping line must submit the ship's manifest, inbound container list, dangerous goods, and special cargo to Sahathai Terminal's documentation office.
DocumentProcess.content2_1: The shipping line or its agent must submit the Booking Forecast, Pre-loading Plan, and Special Stowage Instructions to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA).
DocumentProcess.content2_2: The shipping line or its agent must submit the Final Loading List, Final Loading Summary, and Final Loading Plan (if any) to Sahathai Terminal at least 12 hours before the estimated time of arrival (ETA).
DocumentProcess.content2_3: Once the cargo cut-off time at the container yard has passed, the shipping line or its agent must immediately submit the documents for containers awaiting loading to Sahathai Terminal to prevent delays.
DocumentProcess.content2_4: In the event that the berth is fully booked, the shipping line or its agent must submit the documents for containers awaiting loading to Sahathai Terminal to prevent delays.
